newcomerCriteria: The category is pupils needing Japanese instruction, in primary and lower secondary
Listed circumstances are returnees, foreign pupils, and another language used at home
The criterion is ability: not enough everyday Japanese, OR everyday Japanese without
the grade-level academic language the pupil needs to take part in learning
Special-curriculum instruction is for those needing teaching outside the enrolled class
removalCriteria: Whether Japanese instruction is still needed is judged under the principal's responsibility
Several staff should contribute: the Japanese teacher, class and subject teachers, assistants
They weigh Japanese ability, adaptation to school life, and attitude to learning together
MEXT offers DLA, its dialogic assessment, as one objective measure alongside local methods
Review is periodic: planning at year end, and revisiting at the end of terms
No instrument is named as deciding, and no fixed period runs out

removalCriteria: Hebrew hours run for the first two school years mostly studied in Israel
Arriving before 1 January gives hours that year and the next; after it, that year and two
Upper secondary then keeps one Hebrew hour across the following four years of study
Ethiopian and Bnei Menashe pupils get full hours three years longer, then partial hours
So no single length fits: the clock differs by arrival date, stage and country of origin
Bagrut accommodations are a separate rule, ten years from aliyah and twelve for Ethiopians
The ministry runs programmes aimed at pupils whose eligibility period has already ended
